articles.title: CI/CD for Mobile Apps: Shipping Without the Fear
articles.excerpt: Every mobile team knows the release-day feeling. One developer builds the app on their laptop, someone else signs it, a third person uploads it to the stores, and everyone holds their breath until rev…
articles.body: Every mobile team knows the release-day feeling. One developer builds the app on their laptop, someone else signs it, a third person uploads it to the stores, and everyone holds their breath until review comes back. A mobile CI/CD pipeline exists to end that ritual: every change goes through the same automated steps, in the same order, with the same checks. CI stands for continuous integration, CD for continuous delivery or deployment. In plain terms, the pipeline watches your code, builds the app, runs the tests, signs it, and hands a finished build to testers. What a mobile CI/CD pipeline actually does Think of the pipeline as an assembly line.
articles.author: Tjvex Studio

articles.title: Prevent Cart Desynchronization and Spoofed Telegram Mini App Checkouts in Vue 3
articles.excerpt: Building an e-commerce catalog inside a Telegram Mini App looks straightforward at first glance: render a grid of items in Vue 3, track selected items in local state, and call a payment gateway when t…
articles.body: Building an e-commerce catalog inside a Telegram Mini App looks straightforward at first glance: render a grid of items in Vue 3, track selected items in local state, and call a payment gateway when the user clicks buy. However, embedded WebViews inside iOS and Android Telegram clients introduce strict constraints that ruin naive implementations. If you rely purely on client-side state, user carts vanish every time Telegram reclaims memory or when the user toggles between chat threads. Worse, if your Vue frontend calculates the final order amount and sends that total directly to your bot backend or payment processor, malicious users can open Telegram Web Inspector, tamper with the Pinia store, and purchase high-ticket items for pennies.

articles.title: Editing the 'Before you begin' section so readers don't get stuck at step three
articles.excerpt: When a reader gets stuck at step three of a tutorial, the problem is often not step three. It's the "Before you begin" section, which promised the reader was ready when they weren't. They installed th…
articles.body: When a reader gets stuck at step three of a tutorial, the problem is often not step three. It's the "Before you begin" section, which promised the reader was ready when they weren't. They installed the wrong version, or they don't have the right permission, or the tutorial assumed they knew something it never mentioned. Prerequisites are usually written last and edited least. I've learned to give them a full editing pass of their own. Here's what I look for. Vague items that can't be checked A typical first draft looks like this: ## Prerequisites - Node.js - Docker - A GitHub account - Basic knowledge of the command line Every item is true, and almost none helps. Which Node.js version? Does Docker need to be running, or just installed? What does the GitHub account need to be able to do?

articles.title: Meshy vs GenAnywhere: A Pipeline Guide for Mixing Asset and Site Models
articles.excerpt: A colleague sent me two folders last month. One held a GLB exported from Meshy, a bench with a nice wood texture. The other held a site export from GenAnywhere covering the plaza where the bench was s…
articles.body: A colleague sent me two folders last month. One held a GLB exported from Meshy, a bench with a nice wood texture. The other held a site export from GenAnywhere covering the plaza where the bench was supposed to go. His question was short: make these line up. They do not share a coordinate system, a unit convention, or a lighting model. That is not a defect. The two tools are built for different scales, and the integration work is the same every time. It belongs in the asset pipeline, not in someone's memory. Any 3D pipeline that mixes generated assets with generated sites hits it. The two outputs Meshy: assets Text or image in, mesh out. You get a GLB (glTF) or FBX with PBR maps, several variants, and options to re-mesh or retopologize.

articles.title: BPM Finder Under the Hood: How Tempo Detection Works (With a Python Example)
articles.excerpt: By Tania Alwan Every BPM finder, from a DJ app to an online upload tool, answers the same question: how many beats per minute does this track have? The answer looks like a single number, but it comes…
articles.body: By Tania Alwan Every BPM finder, from a DJ app to an online upload tool, answers the same question: how many beats per minute does this track have? The answer looks like a single number, but it comes out of a small pipeline with a few well-known failure modes. This post walks through that pipeline and shows a short Python example you can run on your own files. Step 1: Turn audio into an onset envelope Tempo detectors rarely look at the raw waveform. They first compute an onset strength envelope: a curve that rises whenever the sound suddenly gets louder or brighter, such as a kick drum, a strum or a new syllable. The signal is cut into short overlapping frames. For each frame, the detector measures how much the spectrum increased compared with the previous frame.

articles.title: Your Mentee Has an Offer to Work for a Manager You Did Not Get On With
articles.excerpt: Your mentee is excited. They have an offer for a role they really want, and they tell you the name of the person they would report to. You know that name. Five years ago you worked for this manager, a…
articles.body: Your mentee is excited. They have an offer for a role they really want, and they tell you the name of the person they would report to. You know that name. Five years ago you worked for this manager, and it was the worst eighteen months of your career. You left partly because of them. Your first instinct may be to warn them off. Hold that for a moment, because what you know is real but narrower than it feels. Start with how old your information is. Five years is a long time. People change, especially after a bad stretch, a new boss of their own, or some honest feedback. The manager you remember may not be the one your mentee would meet. Then separate what happened from how it felt.

The elves Galadriel (Morfydd Clark) and Arondir (Ismael Cruz Córdova) travel into enemy territory with an unreliable guide who doesn’t like elf food and pits the friends against each other, just like Gollum does with Frodo and Sam. Galadriel finds herself hiding in a hedge from a Nazgnagôl, the still-living precursors to the Ringwraiths that would put Frodo and his Hobbit friends in the exact same position. Night Shyamalan has no shortage of horror films that can work in the chilly, dreary days of November, such as 2004's The Village . But an underrated 2015 found-footage horror film manages to cement itself in Shyamalan's filmography as one of his greatest unexpected achievements.
